cards.text: Jacob goes on his way, headed back toward the land he fled when his brother Esau planned to kill him (Genesis 27:41-43). On the road, the angels of God meet him. When an angel showed up at the junk drawer I was stuck in, I asked if he had the right drawer, so let's see if Jacob does any better.

cards.question: Jacob sees the angels of God right there on the road. What does he say?

answers.text: This is the camp of God
This is the gate of heaven
This is the mountain of God

cards.text: So Jacob names that place Mahanaim. Then he sends messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau, in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.

cards.question: In his message to Esau, Jacob calls himself Esau's ___.

cards.text: Jacob's message says he's been staying with Laban, his mother's brother (Genesis 29:10), all this time. Then he lists what he's got now: oxen, donkeys, flocks, menservants and maidservants.

cards.question: Jacob says he's sending this message to Esau so he can find favor in Esau's sight.

cards.text: The messengers come back with news: Esau is coming to meet Jacob. And he's not coming alone.

cards.question: Esau is on his way to meet Jacob. Who's coming with him?

cards.text: FOUR. HUNDRED. MEN. You ever get a text from your boss that just says "call me"? Now multiply that feeling by four hundred, because Jacob is in great fear and distress.

cards.question: Jacob is in great fear and distress, so he divides his people, flocks, herds and camels into two ___.
Jacob's plan with the two camps: if Esau attacks one camp, the other camp can ___.

cards.text: Then Jacob prays. He calls on the God of his father Abraham, the God of his father Isaac, the LORD who told him to go back to his country and promised to make him prosper.

cards.question: In his prayer, Jacob tells God he deserves all the kindness and faithfulness God has shown him.

cards.text: Jacob crossed the Jordan with only his staff, and now he's become two camps. The man left with a STICK and came back needing a SECOND campground.

cards.question: In his prayer, what does Jacob ask God to do?

answers.text: Lead him safely back to Laban
Send the angels to fight for him

cards.question: Jacob tells God he's afraid Esau may come and attack him and the mothers and children with him.

cards.text: Then Jacob wraps up his prayer by reminding God of something God Himself said. I think Jacob's holding on to that promise with both hands.

cards.question: At the end of his prayer, Jacob reminds God of a promise God made him. What is it?

answers.text: Offspring like the sand of the sea
A land flowing with milk and honey
A throne that will last forever

cards.text: Jacob spends the night there. And from everything he brought with him, he picks something out for his brother Esau.

cards.question: From everything he brought with him, Jacob picks out a ___ for his brother Esau.

cards.text: This is no small gift: hundreds of goats, sheep, camels, cows, bulls and donkeys. I can fit a whole batch in one cookie box. Jacob's gift needs its own ROAD.
Jacob hands the animals over to his servants. Then he tells them to go on ahead of him.

cards.question: Jacob's servants are taking the herds on ahead. What does he tell them about the herds?

cards.text: Then Jacob gives the servant in the lead his lines. When Esau meets him and asks whose animals these are, here's what he's supposed to say.

cards.question: Esau asks the lead servant whose animals these are. What is the servant to answer?
The lead servant is also supposed to tell Esau that Jacob is behind them.

cards.text: It's not just the lead servant: the second, the third and every servant after them gets the same speech for Esau. That's not a gift anymore, friend, that's a PARADE with a SCRIPT.

cards.question: Jacob sends the gift ahead of him before he faces Esau. What is he hoping the gift will do?

answers.text: Win Esau over before they meet
Pay Esau for crossing his land
Show Esau how rich Jacob is

cards.question: Jacob is sure that once Esau gets the gifts, Esau will accept him.

cards.text: So Jacob's gifts go on ahead of him, and Jacob spends the night in the camp. Hang on to your apron, friend, because Jacob's story keeps on going.
